_comment: NEGATIVE CONTROL -- not signoff evidence. gf180-bandgap#192.
erc-supply-spec.json's item-11 verdict is 'zero erc.unconnected_net and
zero erc.supply_short'. A count of zero is only meaningful if the rule
that produces it actually ran: a spec whose nets[] were silently dropped
(a typo'd key, a schema change, a label_layer that resolves to nothing)
reports exactly the same zero. This spec is the control that tells those
two cases apart.
It is erc-supply-spec.json verbatim -- same stackup, same vias, same
label_layer -- with ONE extra nets[] entry naming a rail that does not
exist in this layout. The expected result is therefore NOT clean:
erc_finding_count: 1
erc.unconnected_net  net='no_such_rail'
"declared net 'no_such_rail' matches no labelled geometry in this
layout"
status: violations, exit 3
and run_erc.py --expect findings asserts exactly that. If this control
ever comes back clean, the zero in the signoff report has stopped meaning
anything and the item-11 claim must be withdrawn until it is explained.
vdd/vss/vref are carried unchanged so the control also demonstrates that
the real declarations still resolve while the bogus one does not -- one
finding, not four.
